---
title: "Practical resources"

The original brief specifies 53 checklists, decision aids and templates. All 53 are now substantive book pages, linked to the decisions and pause points where they are useful.

The first usable release is a set of checklists organised around **consequential pause points**: moments when a short check can still prevent avoidable harm, rework or an indefensible decision.

## Templates

The 33 templates cover supervision agreements and records; topic, question and contribution due diligence; searching and synthesis; method decisions and deviations; data, file and repository documentation; AI-use records; feedback, authorship and journal decisions; reviewer responses; escalation; and thesis contribution mapping. Browse them in the left book contents under **Practical resources: Templates**.

Priority templates show both a blank structure and a completed example. Each resource explains when to use it, what a defensible entry looks like, and what it cannot decide for you.

The public repository keeps the row-by-row status in [`planning/requirements-checklist.csv`](https://github.com/hareshsuppiah/handbook-for-the-recently-enrolled/blob/main/planning/requirements-checklist.csv).
